_comment: sim-robust-throat-momentum-launch-v1: MERGE into the mission runtime-config (navigation block) ON TOP of the sim-robust-heading-hold-bound-v1 fragment (the PR258 pre-throat alignment gate) and ALL the PR 201/236/250/traction keys (keep them -- they stay the untouched backstop). This fragment ADDS the momentum LAUNCH window. WHY: coldwin18 (2026-10-24, byte-identical to the COMPLETE coldwin16 + the PR258 gate) entered the throat ALIGNED (base_yaw ~ -1 deg, throat_misaligned=0 -- the PR258 yaw cause is removed) but then PINNED FROM REST at x=-3.935 while aligned: at one trace tick the robot linear speed collapsed 0.183 -> 0.006 m/s in 16.7 ms (a ~10 m/s^2 impulse the 200 N drive cannot brake), the hitch articulation dropped 0.1996 -> 0.1987, the whole train sat ~27 s SIM jittering < 0.01 m net, NAV_BREAKAWAY enter x3, rock exhausted -> coupled_no_progress. CPU inspection of the mission.usda around the throat (x=-3.5..-3.935, y=15.25) finds NO door threshold / sill / jamb / wall / floor seam -- the backroom floor is a single flat plane at z=0 and the only colliders in the region are the ceiling (z=4), the east wall (x=1.0) and the TransferBay (north, off the path). So the pin is NOT a modelled collider; it is a from-low-momentum PhysX wheel/caster contact, stochastic across byte-identical runs. The passers (coldwin16, coldwin11, hold2) all rolled THROUGH the same spot at cruise carrying straight-travel momentum; the pinners had just been correcting yaw into the lip, leaving the trailing casters swiveled off-axle so they scrub instead of roll from the near-stop. FIX = complete the PR258 alignment at least heading_hold_launch_m before the throat, then CROSS the pin with STRAIGHT travel (curvature 0, NO steering corrections) at CRUISE so the casters trail and the wheels carry momentum. Every key is opt-in and backward compatible; absent => the prior behaviour byte-identical.
_integration_lane_steps: 1. Merge this navigation block into the mission runtime config (the integration lane owns ~/datasets configs; do NOT hand-edit them via a worker PR). This is the heading-hold-bound block + the two new launch keys.

2. Set RESTOCK_TRACE_CASTERS=1 in the run env so each nav-trace row carries the caster swivel angles + the wheel-contact proxy (so the swivel state at the lip is captured). Keep RESTOCK_NAV_PLAN_DIAG=1 for the NAV_THROAT_LAUNCH / NAV_HEADING_HOLD console lines.

3. Bounded couple+outbound proof from the coldwin18 seat: run_mobile_restock.py --start-at couple --stop-after outbound (the coldwin18 recipe), serialized through flock /tmp/aile-gpu.lock, HEAVY_MB=2500 if whispr holds VRAM, NEVER --force, never touch whispr (pid 1339, ~2.2 GB). Repeat at least twice (the pin was stochastic).

4. Grade each run's nav-trace with the shipped gate: python3 scripts/check_tow_traction.py --environment <env.json> --scenario <mission-scenario.json> --camera-config <camera-config-bay.json> --fragment docs/examples/coupled-traction-fragment.json --runs-dir <mission-dir> --gpu-run <run-dir>. PASS = GPU_RUN PASS with reached_goal=true, single_tick_stops=0 (crosses x=-3.90 with no from-rest collapse), longest_pin_s < escape_s, AND trace_has_casters=true (the new fields present). Also confirm the console has NO 'NAV_BREAKAWAY enter' and NO 'throat_misaligned'. Then the full capstone.

_key_notes.heading_hold_launch_m: float, default 0.0 => the momentum launch is OFF and the PR258 gate is byte-identical. When > 0 (requires heading_hold_prethroat_m > 0 AND heading_hold_launch_m < heading_hold_prethroat_m, so alignment has runway before the launch), the follower command inside the launch window -- within this distance of the throat along the travel axis, EITHER side of the lip so the straight cruise spans the pin -- is overridden, ONCE ALIGNED, to a dead-straight forward cruise (curvature 0, NO steering corrections). A base still misaligned on entry keeps the bounded PR258 alignment gate (creep + saturated corrective turn + align-timeout -> named 'throat_misaligned'), so the launch never fires misaligned and there is never a silent wedge. 0.25 straddles the recorded pin x=-3.935 (0.06 m west of the throat) with margin.
_key_notes.heading_hold_launch_mps: float in [0, 1.0], default 0.0 => use the full coupled speed cap (self.max_speed) as the launch cruise. When > 0, the launch cruise is min(max_speed, this). The launch NEVER reduces the follower's own speed (v = max(follower_v, cruise)) and is FORWARD-only -- it only ADDS momentum, never crawls, never reverses. 0.18 = the passers' measured straight cruise across the same spot.
_key_notes._backstops: PR 201's net-progress monitor (coupled_progress_escape), PR 236's bounded break-away windows and PR 250's rock (coupled_breakaway_rock) stay the UNTOUCHED backstop: the launch only replaces the command while _breakaway_cmd is None, so if a run still pins the rock/fault ladder owns it exactly as before.

_scope_note: This fragment only adds the forward-only momentum launch across the from-rest PhysX throat pin; it does not touch PR 241's lead-in, PR 201's monitor thresholds, PR 236's bound, PR 250's rock, the couple fine-dock, or any cart/caster friction or mass value, and it never commands reverse (mobile.wheel_targets v>=0 / gate_velocity linear>=0, the coupled-reverse interlock, is a separate captain decision and out of scope). The throat has NO modelled collider (CPU-verified); if a future asset review wants a realistic door threshold there, that is a separate asset change -- see the report. Full analysis + the one-tick collapse numbers + the base-front/caster/collider sketch: data/sim-robust-throat-momentum-launch-v1/report.md. CPU proof: scripts/twin/tests/test_outbound_throat_launch.py, scripts/twin/tests/test_navigation_factory.py, scripts/twin/tests/test_tow_traction.py; factory wiring + grader scripts/check_tow_traction.py.
